chunks: ʿUbaydullāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about salat (prayer) on a ship, and he said:

“He should face the qiblah and set his feet properly. If it turns and he is able to turn toward the qiblah, then let him do so; otherwise, let him pray in whatever direction it turns him. If standing is possible for him, then let him pray standing; otherwise, let him sit and then pray.”

key_terms.السَّفِينَةِ: ship, the place where the prayer is being performed
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act being discussed
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةَ: the direction of prayer toward which one should face
key_terms.فَلْيَقْعُدْ: then let him sit, if standing is not possible
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing, as the manner of performing the prayer
key_terms.يَتَوَجَّهَ: to turn oneself or orient oneself toward a direction

ai.seo_question: How should one perform salat (prayer) on a ship if it changes direction?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for performing salat (prayer) on a ship. It instructs the worshipper to face the qiblah when possible, adjust if the vessel turns, and pray according to one's capacity, standing if able and otherwise sitting.
